findings.title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by on line 105 can return nil if the user has never visited the topic (no TopicUser row exists). Line 107 then calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError. This will happen when a user clicks the unsubscribe link in an email for a topic they were notified about but never actually opened in the browser. A nil check or use of TopicUser.change (which handles upsert) is needed.

findings.title: State-changing action exposed via GET request enables CSRF
findings.body: The unsubscribe route is defined as a GET request (get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe") but the controller action mutates the notification_level. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests. An attacker can embed or a link in any page/email to silently change a user's notification level. Browsers, link previewers, and crawlers may also trigger this unintentionally. This should be a POST/PUT route with CSRF token verification.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url, breaking other callers
findings.body: The unsubscribe_link locale string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Any code path that calls build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true but does not pass unsubscribe_url in opts will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at runtime. While the current notification email path provides it, plugins or future code using add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url will break. A default or conditional interpolation should be considered.

findings.title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The property is named stopNotificiationsText (with an extra 'i' — 'Notificiations' instead of 'Notifications'). While it is used consistently in the template so it won't cause a runtime error, it introduces a confusing misspelling that will trip up future developers searching for 'notification' in the codebase.

findings.title: No controller spec for the unsubscribe action
findings.body: The unsubscribe action introduces new behavior (mutating notification level, redirecting on slug mismatch, rendering the topic view) but has no corresponding controller spec. The nil TopicUser bug and the GET-based state mutation would both be caught by basic request specs. At minimum, tests should cover: successful unsubscribe when TopicUser exists, behavior when TopicUser is missing, and slug mismatch redirect.

findings.title: Triple-mustache renders unescaped HTML including user-controlled topic title
findings.body: The template uses {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} (triple mustache, no escaping). The value includes model.fancyTitle which is HTML-escaped server-side via ERB::Util.html_escape, so it is currently safe. However, this creates a fragile dependency: if fancyTitle is ever changed to not escape, or if a different title property is substituted, this becomes an XSS vector. A safer pattern would be to use a component or helper that explicitly marks only the <strong> wrapper as safe.
